sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that due to inadvertence the crime number has not been mentioned and incomplete details of offence are mentioned in the first page of memo of bail application.
Though, in para no.3, description of all the offence are mentioned .

Considering the aforesaid, learned counsel for applicant is permitted to carry out necessary amendment in the first page of memo during the course of the day in the court itself and the office is directed to scan the same.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail to the applicant,
relating to FIR/Crime No.251/2023 registered at P.S. Kathhiwara, District Alirajpur (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 409, 120-B of IPC, sec. 74 of IT Act and section 13(1)(a) and 13(1)(b) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

sentences.text: It is argued that the identically placed co-accused persons namely Shyam Rathore in M.Cr.C No.4078/2024 and Vikas Rathore in M.Cr.C No.4088/2024 have been granted bail.
It is alleged that accused persons alongwith co-accused persons have misappropriated Government fund to the tune of Rs.86,36,455/-which was meant for the purpose of meting the school expenses.
Counsel for the applicant submits that there are total 6 accused persons including Block Education Officers, Accountant and Assistant Teachers.
It is submitted that 4 Block Education Officers and Accountant have been granted anticipatory bail by the trial court.
It is argued that applicant is neither Govt. servant nor his name was mentioned in the FIR.
According to the prosecution,it is alleged that amount was transferred to his account and the allegation is that applicant conspired and facilitated the commission of offence.
It is argued that there is no entrustment of public money as applicant is not Government servant.
The Drawing and Disbursing Officers have already been granted anticipatory bail by the trial court.

Counsel for the State opposed the prayer submitting that a huge amount was transferred in the bank account of present applicant, his wife and co- accused and major part of the amount has already been withdrawn by them.
After hearing learned counsel for parties and taking into consideration that applicant is neither Govt. servant nor Drawing and Disbursing Officer, the Block Education Officers who are Drawing and Disbursing Officer have already been granted anticipatory bail by the trial court, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that the applicant- Sapnesh Rathore be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for securing his presence before the said Court regularly on all the dates fixed in this regard during trial on the condition that applicant shall not operate his bank account in question without the permission of the trial court.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE Sourabh Sapnesh Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59625223/
